final_answer: Hypothesis: Increased education spending does not positively impact per capita GDP in either Sub-Saharan Africa or Lower Middle Income countries. In fact, the relationship appears to be negative in both regions, although the relationship is stronger in Sub-Saharan Africa. This hypothesis is based on the dataset provided, which includes data on education expenditure and per capita GDP for these regions from 1975 to 2015. The variables chosen for the analysis are 'Adjusted savings: education expenditure (percentage of GNI)' and 'GNI per capita (constant 2015 US dollar)'. The relationship between these variables is negative, as indicated by the negative coefficients in the linear regression analysis. The statistical significance of the relationship is supported by the high R-squared value for Sub-Saharan Africa (0.934) and the moderate R-squared value for Lower Middle Income countries (0.231).
